sets.context: A student reserves a soundproof booth for group work.

sentences.text: The study booths are on the second floor.
You can reserve one online for two hours.
Each booth has a screen and four chairs.
Bring your student card to unlock the door.
Please cancel online if your group no longer needs the booth.
Food is not allowed inside, but covered drinks are fine during your study session.
Use the phone by the stairs to contact library staff if the screen is not working.

sets.context: A science student collects required clothing before a lab session.

sentences.text: Your lab coat is ready at the front desk.
Please bring your student ID when you collect it.
You can try on the coat before taking it upstairs.
Ask the staff for another size if this one feels tight.
Write your name inside the collar so coats do not get mixed up.
After each lab, place the used coat in the laundry bin beside the exit.
Request a replacement from the science office if you lose your coat during the semester.

sets.context: A learner checks in for a short peer tutoring appointment.

sentences.text: Your tutor is waiting in room twelve.
Sign in on the tablet near the entrance.
Bring the assignment you want to discuss today.
The first few minutes are for explaining what you find difficult.
Your tutor can review your ideas, but cannot complete the work for you.
At the end, you will choose one skill to practice before your next appointment.
Book another session online instead of extending this one if you need more time.

sets.context: Volunteers divide the watering jobs in a student garden.

sentences.text: The watering cans are beside the greenhouse.
Today, your group will water the vegetable beds.
Fill each can only halfway so it is easier to carry.
Pour water near the roots rather than over the leaves.
The herb garden is already wet, so please leave that area alone.
When both vegetable beds are finished, return the empty cans to the wooden shelf.
Tell the garden leader before the group leaves if you notice a broken plant marker.

sets.context: A club member gets an event poster approved before posting it.

sentences.text: Bring your poster to the student activities desk.
We approve posters between ten and four.
The event date and club name must be easy to see.
Remove any outside company logos before you submit the design.
Once approved, the poster will receive a small blue stamp.
You may hang copies on general boards, but classroom doors require separate permission.
Posters without an approval stamp are removed each Friday during the regular building check.

sets.context: A music student borrows a key for an individual practice room.

sentences.text: Practice room keys are kept at the music desk.
Leave your student card while you use the key.
The room number is printed on the key tag.
Most practice sessions are limited to one hour during busy periods.
Please use headphones if you are connecting an electronic instrument.
When your session ends, close the windows and switch off the room lights.
Return the key directly to the desk so the next student can start on time.

sets.context: A student identifies a notebook at the campus lost-property desk.

sentences.text: We found several notebooks in the library yesterday.
Tell me the color and subject of yours.
Describe the cover without opening any of the notebooks.
I may ask about a note written on the first page.
Once we identify it, you will sign the lost property record.
Items that nobody claims are stored here for thirty days before being donated.
Leave your contact details and we will call you if this is not your notebook.

sets.context: A student picks up a printed packet for a new seminar.

sentences.text: The seminar packets are on the counter.
Take the copy with your section number.
The reading schedule is printed on the first page.
You will need the case study for Thursday morning.
Some pages are double-sided, so count them before leaving the office.
If your packet is missing a page, exchange it here rather than printing another copy.
Please write your name on the cover because every section uses the same blue packet.

sets.context: A commuter registers a bicycle for a covered campus rack.

sentences.text: Covered bike parking requires a campus permit.
Register your bicycle online with its serial number.
We will attach the permit below your seat.
Only registered bicycles may stay in the covered racks overnight.
The permit is free, but you need to provide your own lock.
Bicycles left outside the marked spaces may be moved to the security office.
Remove the permit and update your registration before transferring ownership if you sell your bike.

sets.context: A residence adviser explains evening rules for a quiet floor.

sentences.text: This is the residence hall quiet floor.
Quiet hours begin at nine every evening.
Please take phone calls to the lounge or stairwell.
Headphones are required when you watch videos in your room.
The study room stays open late for silent individual work.
On weekends, guests are welcome, but the same noise rules still apply.
Contact the adviser instead of confronting the resident if noise from another room continues.

sets.context: A resident borrows a basic tool from a community lending shelf.

sentences.text: The tool shelf is open to neighborhood residents.
You can borrow two tools for one week.
Show your library card at the service window.
We inspect each tool with you before you take it home.
Power tools include instructions and must be returned with their chargers.
If a tool stops working, bring it back without trying to repair it yourself.
Popular garden tools can be reserved online, especially during the first weeks of spring.

sets.context: A volunteer collects bags and gloves for a park cleanup.

sentences.text: Gloves and trash bags are available at this table.
Choose a route from the park map.
Place glass and sharp objects in the red bucket.
Full trash bags should be left beside the main path.
Recycling goes into clear bags, while other waste goes into black ones.
Please work with a partner near the river because the ground can be slippery.
When you finish your route, return here so we can record which areas were cleaned.

sets.context: A resident prepares chairs for a neighborhood discussion.

sentences.text: Tonight’s discussion will use the large community room.
Set up six rows of eight chairs.
Leave a wide path along the left wall.
The front row should include space for two wheelchairs.
Put the sign-in table just inside the main entrance.
After arranging the chairs, test the microphone and place water near the speaker’s seat.
When the meeting ends, stack the chairs in groups of ten beside the storage door.

sets.context: A visitor receives a number for a weekly food pickup.

sentences.text: Please take a number from the green machine.
We call five households into the pantry at once.
Keep your number visible while you wait in the hall.
A volunteer will explain today’s choices when your group enters.
Cold food is collected last so it stays at a safe temperature.
If you cannot carry everything home, we have small carts you may borrow.
Families who miss their number can join the final group after regular pickup ends.

sets.context: A tenant requests a replacement bin from a local office.

sentences.text: Replacement recycling bins are available from the local office.
Tell us whether your bin is damaged or missing.
A damaged bin can be exchanged without a fee.
Bring the old bin here or request pickup from your building.
New bins usually arrive within five working days after approval.
Until then, place clean recycling in a clear bag beside your other container.
The property manager must submit the replacement request if your building uses shared bins.

sets.context: A neighbor joins a weekly morning walking group.

sentences.text: The walking group meets here every Saturday morning.
There is no fee to join.
Write your phone number on the sign-up sheet.
Most walks last about an hour and follow paved paths.
Wear comfortable shoes and bring water during warm weather.
The group leaves at eight thirty, so please arrive a few minutes early.
When heavy rain is expected, the leader sends a cancellation message by seven that morning.

sets.context: A volunteer helps translate a short public notice.

sentences.text: This notice explains the new parking hours.
We need a clear translation by Wednesday.
Please keep street names in their original form.
Use short sentences that are easy for residents to understand.
The phone number at the bottom should appear in every language.
Another volunteer will review your draft before the translated notice is printed.
Add a brief explanation in parentheses if a local term has no direct translation.

sets.context: A parent asks when a neighborhood playground will reopen.

sentences.text: The playground is closed while workers replace the surface.
The work should finish next Friday.
The small park across Oak Street remains open.
New fencing will be installed after the ground is dry.
We will post the reopening date on the community website.
Although the swings are finished, families must stay outside until the safety inspection is complete.
The notice at both entrances will show the revised date if bad weather delays the inspection.

sets.context: A volunteer confirms a meal delivery route for older residents.

sentences.text: Your first lunch delivery is on Pine Street.
The meals are packed in route order.
Ring the bell and wait for someone to answer.
If nobody answers, call the number on your route sheet.
Return empty delivery bags to the center after your final stop.
Several residents have limited hearing, so give them extra time to reach the door.
Contact the coordinator before continuing with the rest of your route if a resident seems unwell.

sets.context: A volunteer checks in before a neighborhood tree planting event.

sentences.text: Tree planting volunteers should check in at this tent.
We will assign you to a small team.
Pick up gloves and a name tag here.
Your team leader will demonstrate how deep to dig each hole.
Young trees need loose soil and plenty of water around their roots.
After planting, tie the tree gently to its support and add a layer of soil cover.
Before leaving, record the tree number so volunteers can water it throughout the summer.

sets.context: A passenger adds credit to a city bus pass.

sentences.text: You can reload your bus pass at this machine.
First, place the card on the blue circle.
Choose an amount and pay by cash or card.
The new balance will appear on the screen after payment.
Take the receipt if you need proof for work or school.
Online payments may take several minutes to appear when you board the next bus.
Bring the receipt to the transit office for a refund if the machine charges you twice.

sets.context: A traveler learns that a train will leave from another platform.

sentences.text: The northbound train will leave from platform six.
Platform four is closed for repairs.
Follow the yellow signs through the main hall.
The elevator to platform six is beside the ticket office.
Your departure time has not changed, despite the platform move.
Passengers needing assistance should speak to station staff before going through the gate.
Listen for another announcement because late track work could cause one more platform change.

sets.context: A hotel guest locates the correct airport shuttle stop.

sentences.text: The airport shuttle stops behind the hotel.
Use the glass doors beside the restaurant.
The stop is marked with a purple airport sign.
Shuttles leave every thirty minutes from early morning until midnight.
Tell the driver which terminal you need before loading your bag.
During busy hours, hotel guests should arrive at the stop at least ten minutes early.
The front desk can reserve a seat on the next one if the shuttle is full.

sets.context: A cyclist asks where to leave a bicycle during a ferry ride.

sentences.text: Bicycles board the ferry through the rear gate.
A crew member will direct you to the rack.
Remove loose bags before securing your bicycle.
Straps are attached to the wall beside each parking space.
You may leave your helmet with the bicycle during the crossing.
Return to the vehicle deck only after the crew announces that it is open.
Cyclists leave after cars, so wait beside your bicycle until a crew member signals.

sets.context: A passenger requests a partial refund after a long train delay.

sentences.text: Your train arrived more than two hours late.
That delay qualifies for a partial refund.
Please show your ticket and payment card.
We will confirm the arrival time in our system.
Refunds return to the original payment method within five business days.
If someone else bought the ticket, the money will go back to that person’s account.
Keep this claim number until the refund appears, in case customer service needs more details.

sets.context: A driver returns a shared car to a designated area.

sentences.text: Return the shared car to zone three.
Park in any space marked with a green sign.
Take your belongings and remove any trash.
The fuel tank should be at least one quarter full.
End the rental in the app after locking every door.
If the return zone is full, photograph the car and call the support number.
Do not leave the car in a public space unless a support agent approves the location.

sets.context: A commuter finds a temporary bus stop during road work.

sentences.text: The regular bus stop is closed this week.
Use the temporary stop outside the bank.
It is about two blocks past the construction area.
A blue sign shows where passengers should form a line.
All routes from the old stop will use this location.
Allow extra walking time because the bus cannot wait near the road work.
The regular stop will reopen Monday morning unless construction takes longer than expected.

sets.context: A traveler stores a small bag in a station locker.

sentences.text: Small lockers are available near the station entrance.
Choose an empty locker with a green light.
Place your bag inside and close the door firmly.
The screen will ask you to create a six-digit code.
Your locker number appears on the receipt after you pay.
You can open the locker once during the rental without paying a second fee.
Station staff will need identification before releasing your bag if you forget the code.

sets.context: A passenger confirms an accessible taxi pickup point.

sentences.text: Your accessible taxi will use the east entrance.
The pickup point is beside the wide ramp.
Your driver is expected at two fifteen.
A text message will include the car number when it arrives.
There is covered seating next to the pickup area.
If you use a wheelchair, tell the driver whether it folds before they secure it.
Call the booking line if the taxi is more than ten minutes late or stops elsewhere.

sets.context: A rider returns a rented scooter within the marked area.

sentences.text: Rental scooters must be returned inside a marked zone.
The nearest zone is beside the public library.
Park the scooter upright between the painted lines.
Do not block the sidewalk, doorway, or bicycle rack.
Take a clear photo after lowering the stand.
The app will end your ride only when it recognizes the correct parking area.
When the zone is full, use the map to find another approved parking area.

sets.context: A customer exchanges a jacket for a different size.

sentences.text: This jacket is available in two larger sizes.
You may try them on in the back fitting room.
Please bring the receipt to the exchange counter.
The tags must still be attached to the jacket.
If the new size costs the same, no additional payment is needed.
We can order another color for home delivery if it is unavailable in the store.
Sale jackets may be exchanged within fourteen days, but we cannot return them for cash.

sets.context: A shopper collects a prepaid grocery order.

sentences.text: Prepaid grocery orders are on the chilled pickup shelf.
Enter your order number on this screen.
A staff member will bring out your bags.
Frozen items are packed separately in a blue bag.
Please compare the number of bags with your order message.
If an item was unavailable, the receipt will show its replacement or refund.
Tell us about any missing item before leaving so we can correct the order immediately.

sets.context: A customer asks about a small discount on a display lamp.

sentences.text: This lamp was used in our window display.
It has a small mark near the base.
We can reduce the price by fifteen percent.
The shade and light bulb are included in the sale.
Display items still have the same one-year electrical guarantee.
You may test the lamp at the counter before deciding whether to buy it.
Because it is the final one, we cannot replace it with an identical lamp later.

sets.context: A reader collects a book ordered through a local shop.

sentences.text: The book you ordered arrived this morning.
It is being held under your last name.
Please collect it from the desk near the entrance.
You can pay the remaining balance when you pick it up.
We will hold the order until the store closes next Tuesday.
The cover has a slight bend, so we can request another copy if you prefer.
We will apply a small discount at the register if you want this copy today.

sets.context: A shopper returns empty jars to receive a deposit.

sentences.text: These glass jars have a refundable deposit.
Rinse the empty jars before bringing them back.
The lids can go in the metal recycling bin.
Place each clean jar in the return machine carefully.
The machine prints a credit slip after counting your jars.
Use the slip at any register today, or save it for your next visit.
Cracked jars cannot enter the machine, but staff can dispose of them safely.

sets.context: A customer leaves a pair of shoes for a simple repair.

sentences.text: We can replace the worn heel on these shoes.
The repair should take about four days.
This ticket shows your collection date and price.
Bring the ticket when you return for the shoes.
We will call if we find damage under the old heel.
You do not need to pay for additional work unless you approve it first.
When you collect the shoes, try them on so we can check the repaired height.

sets.context: A shopper chooses a weekly box of local produce.

sentences.text: Our produce boxes are packed every Thursday.
The small box is suitable for one person.
This week it contains apples, carrots, beans, and lettuce.
You may exchange one item at the market table.
Orders placed by Tuesday are ready for Friday pickup.
The contents change with the season, so next week’s box may be quite different.
We will reuse it for a future order if you bring back the empty box.

sets.context: A customer gets help measuring a window for curtains.

sentences.text: Measure the width of the window in three places.
Use the smallest measurement when ordering curtains.
Next, measure from the rail to the floor.
Add extra width if you want the fabric to look full.
This guide shows where to place the end of the tape.
Bring your measurements and a photo of the window when you visit the curtain desk.
Choose the rail before ordering curtains, since its height determines the final curtain length.

sets.context: A shopper tests a toy before giving it as a gift.

sentences.text: We can test the toy at this counter.
It requires three small batteries.
Open the battery cover with this screwdriver.
Make sure the positive ends face the marked direction.
Press the red button to test the lights and sound.
The batteries are sold separately, but we can install them before gift wrapping.
Choose another one from the shelf if the toy does not work after the test.

sets.context: A customer returns an online purchase at a store counter.

sentences.text: Online purchases can be returned at this counter.
Show me the order email on your phone.
The item should be unused and in its original box.
We will scan the code beside the product name.
You can choose a refund or store credit today.
Shipping charges are refunded only when the item arrived damaged or incorrect.
It may take several days to receive the money if you paid through another service.

sets.context: A customer arranges collection of a prepaid bread order.

sentences.text: Your bread order will be ready after three.
Collect it from the side counter.
Give the staff your name and order number.
The rolls will be packed separately from the sliced bread.
We keep prepaid orders until one hour before closing.
If you arrive earlier, we can prepare the items that have already cooled.
Call the bakery if you are delayed, and we will hold the order until tomorrow morning.

sets.context: A customer changes the milk choice on a drink order.

sentences.text: You can change the milk in your drink.
We have soy, oat, and regular milk.
Oat milk costs a little extra in large drinks.
I will update the order before the barista starts it.
Your name will be called at the pickup end of the counter.
Because the drink contains chocolate sauce, changing the milk will not make it dairy-free.
Tell the barista about any allergy so they can clean the equipment before making your drink.

sets.context: A diner asks how refills work at a lunch counter.

sentences.text: Soup refills are included with the lunch meal.
Bring your bowl back to this counter.
You may choose the same soup or today’s other flavor.
Please leave your tray at the table while getting a refill.
Bread is included only with the first bowl of soup.
The refill offer ends at two, when the lunch counter closes for cleaning.
We can replace it with a small side salad if the soup you want runs out.

sets.context: A subscriber replaces one item in a weekly farm box.

sentences.text: You may replace one item in your farm box.
This week, the extra choices are potatoes and pears.
Mark your choice in the online account by Tuesday.
Items of similar value can be exchanged without a fee.
We cannot change boxes after they have been packed on Thursday.
If you have a food allergy, contact us to remove that item from every order.
When a substitute is unavailable, we will add credit to the following week’s box.

sets.context: A group keeps prepared food safe before an outdoor picnic.

sentences.text: The picnic food is packed in two coolers.
Keep the coolers indoors until the group leaves.
Place meat and dairy products beside the ice packs.
Drinks can go in the smaller cooler near the door.
At the park, keep both coolers closed and out of direct sunlight.
Serve the cold dishes first, then return any unused portions to the cooler promptly.
Food that stays outside for more than two hours should be thrown away, even if it looks fine.

sets.context: A diner joins a short wait list for an evening table.

sentences.text: The current wait for a table is twenty minutes.
I can add your name to the list.
Please tell me how many people are in your party.
We will send a text when your table is nearly ready.
You can wait outside or visit the shop next door.
After receiving the message, return within ten minutes or we may offer the table to another group.
The wait may be shorter, but those tables do not have heaters if you prefer outdoor seating.

sets.context: A participant checks which ingredients are provided.

sentences.text: We provide all the basic cooking ingredients.
Please bring an apron and a food container.
Knives and cutting boards are already at each station.
Tonight’s recipe includes eggs, milk, wheat, and nuts.
Tell the instructor about any allergy before the class begins.
You will work with a partner, but each person will prepare a separate dish.
At the end, label your container before placing leftovers in the shared refrigerator.

sets.context: An employee receives a snack delivery for a small meeting.

sentences.text: The meeting snacks have arrived at reception.
There are three boxes and one drink bag.
Check that the vegetarian box has a green label.
The cold drinks should go into the kitchen refrigerator.
Napkins and cups are packed beneath the fruit tray.
Please arrange the snacks in the small meeting room before the guests arrive.
Call the delivery company using the number on the receipt if anything is missing.

sets.context: A customer follows instructions for heating a prepared meal.

sentences.text: Remove the meal from its cardboard sleeve.
Leave the clear film partly attached.
Heat the meal for three minutes on high.
Stir the vegetables, then heat it for another minute.
Let the container stand before removing the film completely.
Because microwave power varies, make sure the center is hot before you begin eating.
Add one minute to each heating stage if the meal was frozen after purchase.

sets.context: A shopper uses a cashless payment point at a fruit stand.

sentences.text: This fruit stand accepts card and phone payments.
Place your basket on the scale.
The screen will show the total price.
Choose your payment method and follow the instructions.
A green light means the payment has been accepted.
If you need a receipt, enter your email address before removing the basket.
When the screen shows an error, ask the market worker instead of trying the payment repeatedly.

sets.context: A customer leaves a phone for a same-day screen repair.

sentences.text: We can replace your phone screen today.
The repair usually takes about three hours.
Please unlock the phone so we can test it.
We will inspect the camera and buttons before you leave.
Your photos and apps should remain on the phone during this repair.
We will text this number when the new screen has been fitted and tested.
We will explain the extra cost before continuing if we find damage inside the phone.

sets.context: A resident adds money to a shared laundry card.

sentences.text: You can add laundry credit at this machine.
Insert your card with the arrow facing up.
Choose five, ten, or twenty dollars on the screen.
The machine accepts bank cards but not cash.
Wait until the new balance appears before removing your laundry card.
One wash costs two dollars, and the dryers charge by each ten-minute period.
Bring both cards and the receipt to the housing office if the balance does not update.

sets.context: A resident schedules a second delivery for a missed parcel.

sentences.text: We missed you during yesterday’s parcel delivery.
You can choose a new delivery day online.
Enter the number printed below the barcode.
Morning and afternoon delivery windows are available in your area.
Someone over eighteen must sign for this particular parcel.
You may also send it to a nearby collection point that stays open later.
Delivery will take an extra day while we update the label if you change the address.

sets.context: A client adds a simple request to a haircut booking.

sentences.text: Your haircut is booked for Saturday at eleven.
I can add a note for the stylist.
Tell me what you would like changed this time.
The note will appear beside your name in the schedule.
Bring a photo if you want to show a particular length or shape.
Please arrive with dry hair unless your appointment includes a wash and style.
Call us because the current appointment may be too short if you need a longer service.

sets.context: A tenant collects a copy of an apartment key.

sentences.text: Your new apartment key is ready for collection.
Please show identification at the front desk.
The key number will be recorded under your name.
Try the key in the lobby door before going upstairs.
Only the named tenant may collect copies for this apartment.
If the key does not turn smoothly, bring it back and we will cut another copy.
There is a replacement fee for lost keys because the building record must also be updated.

sets.context: A customer confirms when a home internet worker will arrive.

sentences.text: The internet worker will come on Tuesday.
Your arrival window is between noon and four.
An adult needs to be home during the visit.
Please clear the area around the main cable outlet.
The worker will call about thirty minutes before arriving.
If access to the building requires a code, add it to your appointment notes today.
You can change the visit without a fee until six o’clock on Monday evening.

sets.context: A customer leaves a watch for a new battery.

sentences.text: We can replace the battery in this watch.
The service takes about twenty minutes.
I will note the scratch already on the back.
We test the seal after fitting the new battery.
This model should not go underwater unless it passes that test.
The battery has a one-year guarantee, so keep the dated receipt with the watch box.
The movement may need a separate repair by a specialist if the watch still loses time.

sets.context: A customer collects a small batch of printed photos.

sentences.text: Your photo prints are ready in this envelope.
There should be twenty-four standard prints.
Please look through them before leaving the counter.
The larger copies are protected by a sheet of cardboard.
You can request a free reprint if any image is damaged.
Digital copies remain in your account for thirty days after the order is collected.
We can adjust one sample before reprinting everything if the colors look different from your screen.

sets.context: A customer points out a stain when leaving a coat for cleaning.

sentences.text: Please show me where the stain is on the coat.
I will mark that spot on the cleaning tag.
Do you know what caused the stain?
That information helps us choose a safer cleaning method.
The coat will be ready for collection next Wednesday afternoon.
We cannot promise complete removal, but we will avoid treatments that could damage the fabric.
When you collect it, inspect the marked area before we remove the cleaning tag.

sets.context: A resident reports a home water meter reading.

sentences.text: The water meter is outside beside your back door.
Read the five black numbers from left to right.
Do not include the smaller red numbers.
You can report the reading by phone or online.
A clear photo is helpful if the number seems unusually high.
Please submit the reading by Friday so your next bill uses actual water use.
Contact us and we will arrange a visit if you cannot reach the meter safely.

sets.context: A visitor learns where to place a chair at an outdoor film.

sentences.text: Place low chairs in the area near the screen.
Taller chairs belong behind the white line.
Blankets may be spread on the grass at either side.
Please keep the center path clear for people arriving late.
The film begins at sunset, but seating opens at six thirty.
If you leave during the film, use the side path so you do not block the picture.
In case of rain, staff will announce the indoor location on the event page by five.

sets.context: A seller checks in before setting up a craft fair table.

sentences.text: Vendors should check in at the red tent.
Give us your name and table number.
A volunteer will show you the closest unloading space.
Move your car after unloading so other sellers can enter.
Each table includes two chairs but no electrical connection.
You may begin setting up at seven, and all displays must be ready by nine.
Before the fair opens, keep boxes beneath your table and clear the public walkway.

sets.context: A participant joins the speaking order at a poetry event.

sentences.text: The poetry reading begins at seven tonight.
Add your name to the list near the stage.
Each reader has up to four minutes.
The host will introduce the next two speakers in order.
Please sit near the front when your name is coming up.
If you decide not to read, cross out your name so the queue keeps moving.
Anyone joining after the event starts will be placed near the end of the list.

sets.context: A walker collects an entry wristband before a charity route.

sentences.text: Your wristband shows that you checked in.
Wear it until you finish the charity walk.
The blue band is for the longer route.
Water stations are marked on the map inside your packet.
Show the wristband to receive a drink or first-aid help.
At the finish, volunteers will scan its code to record your completed distance.
Tell the volunteer where the two paths separate if you switch to the shorter route.

sets.context: An audience member confirms seating for a public history talk.

sentences.text: Your seats for the history talk are in row six.
The doors open thirty minutes before the program.
Show your booking email at the main entrance.
Unclaimed seats may be released five minutes before the talk.
A question period will follow the speaker’s presentation.
Please use the side entrance if you arrive late because the front doors will be closed.
The talk is being recorded, so audience questions may appear on the library website.

sets.context: A participant checks what shoes to bring to a dance workshop.

sentences.text: Wear shoes that stay firmly on your feet.
Clean indoor sneakers are a good choice.
Please do not wear sandals or high heels.
The studio floor can be slippery in outdoor shoes.
You may dance in socks during the warm-up if you prefer.
Bring a second pair and change in the hall before entering the main studio.
Tell the instructor about any ankle problem so the movements can be adjusted for you.

sets.context: A visitor reserves a table for a community game night.

sentences.text: Game night tables can seat up to six people.
Your group has table four from seven.
Board games are available from the shelves by the window.
You may also bring a game from home.
Return borrowed pieces to the correct box before choosing another game.
If your group finishes early, other players may join your table for the next round.
The final games must begin by nine thirty because the community room closes at eleven.

sets.context: A visitor picks up a route map for a guided river walk.

sentences.text: This map shows the full river walk.
The group starts at the old bridge.
Restrooms are available near the halfway point.
A dotted line marks the shorter return route.
The guide will stop twice to discuss local plants and wildlife.
Stay on the path near the wetland, where the ground beyond the signs is protected.
Before leaving the group early, tell the guide and follow the marked route back.

sets.context: A guest receives a program and seating directions for a school play.

sentences.text: Your seats are in the middle section.
An usher will help you find row eight.
The program includes the cast list and two short breaks.
Please silence phones before the stage lights go down.
Photography is allowed only after the final performance ends.
During each break, use the rear doors because actors enter through the side hall.
Sit near the aisle to avoid interrupting the audience if you need to leave early.

sets.context: A new singer gets directions for a community choir rehearsal.

sentences.text: Choir rehearsal takes place in the school music room.
New singers should arrive at six forty-five.
Pick up a name tag and music folder by the piano.
The director will listen briefly to determine your vocal section.
You do not need to prepare a song for the first rehearsal.
During the break, return borrowed music to the folder so pages do not get lost.
After rehearsal, the director will explain how to access practice recordings from home.

sets.context: An employee replaces paper at a shared office printer.

sentences.text: The shared printer is out of paper.
Extra paper is stored in the lower cabinet.
Open the front tray and move the guides outward.
Place one package of paper between the guides.
Do not fill above the line marked inside the tray.
After closing it, print one test page to make sure the paper feeds correctly.
Contact office support rather than opening another tray if the warning remains on the screen.

sets.context: A receptionist explains how a visitor should return a badge.

sentences.text: Please wear your visitor badge inside the building.
The badge opens only the main office door.
Your host must accompany you in other areas.
Return the badge to reception before leaving today.
If the desk is closed, drop it into the silver box.
Do not give the badge to another visitor because it is registered under your name.
Security will deactivate it at six, even if it has not yet been returned.

sets.context: A coworker adds a changed meeting time to a team calendar.

sentences.text: Tomorrow’s team meeting now begins at ten.
I have changed the time on the shared calendar.
The meeting room remains the same.
Everyone should receive an automatic update by email.
Please accept the new invitation so we know you have seen it.
The client will join for the final fifteen minutes using the link in the calendar.
Remove the old event before accepting the invitation again if the update does not appear.

sets.context: A worker moves supplies through an office without blocking a hall.

sentences.text: Use the service elevator with the delivery cart.
The main hallway is busy until ten.
Enter through the loading area behind the building.
Keep the cart on the right side of each corridor.
Stop beside office doors rather than in front of them.
Deliver the boxes on the third floor first because that office closes early today.
After the last delivery, return the empty cart to the marked space near the elevator.

sets.context: A new employee collects a headset for online meetings.

sentences.text: Your new headset is in this box.
It connects to the computer through the USB port.
The mute button is on the left ear piece.
Use the test call to adjust the microphone level.
A small light turns red whenever your microphone is muted.
For clearer sound, position the microphone near your mouth without letting it touch your face.
Select the headset instead of the computer speakers in your meeting settings if callers hear an echo.

sets.context: Coworkers check who will clean a shared kitchen.

sentences.text: The kitchen cleaning schedule is posted by the sink.
Each team is responsible for one week.
This week, the design team empties the dishwasher.
Wipe the counters each afternoon and replace the hand towel.
Friday’s team should also clear old food from the refrigerator.
If you exchange weeks with another team, write the change directly on the posted schedule.
Cleaning supplies are in the locked cabinet, and the office manager has the key.

sets.context: An employee passes a client file to a coworker securely.

sentences.text: This client file belongs to the north office.
Please give it directly to Maria.
The blue section contains private financial details.
Use the sealed folder while carrying it between buildings.
Maria will sign the handoff sheet when she receives the file.
If she is away, place the folder in her locked cabinet rather than on the desk.
Bring the signed sheet back today so our office can update the file record.

sets.context: A manager posts a short notice about a temporary room closure.

sentences.text: The break room will be closed tomorrow morning.
Workers are repairing the sink and floor.
Please use the small kitchen on level two.
Move any food you need from the refrigerator today.
The coffee machine will remain available in the main lobby.
We expect the room to reopen after lunch, once the new floor is dry.
An updated notice will be posted by noon if the repair takes longer than planned.

sets.context: Coworkers share responsibility for watering office plants.

sentences.text: The office plants are watered twice a week.
Your team is responsible every Tuesday.
Use the small green can beside the sink.
The plants near the windows need less water in winter.
Pour out any water left in the trays after ten minutes.
If a plant has yellow leaves, add a note to the schedule instead of giving it extra water.
The facilities team handles larger plants, so please water only those marked with blue labels.

sets.context: An employee checks access to a remote meeting before it starts.

sentences.text: The meeting link is in today’s calendar event.
Open it before the meeting to test access.
You may need to sign in with your work account.
The waiting room opens ten minutes before the scheduled start.
Choose computer audio unless you plan to join by phone.
If the link opens an old meeting, refresh the calendar and use the updated invitation.
Anyone presenting slides should join early enough to confirm that screen sharing is enabled.

sets.context: A resident changes a mailing address on a local record.

sentences.text: You can update your mailing address at this counter.
Please provide the old and new addresses.
We also need a document showing where you live now.
The change will appear in our records within two days.
Your current card remains valid and does not need replacement.
Mail already sent to the old address cannot be redirected by this office.
Include every family member who moved with you on the same address update form.

sets.context: An applicant collects a receipt after paying a small permit fee.

sentences.text: This receipt confirms your permit fee was paid.
The permit number appears in the top corner.
Keep the receipt until the permit arrives by mail.
Processing usually takes seven to ten business days.
You can use the number to track the application online.
If the permit does not arrive within two weeks, contact us with this payment date.
A duplicate receipt is available later, but you will need identification and the permit number.

sets.context: A visitor corrects a spelling error on an official card.

sentences.text: Your last name is spelled incorrectly on this card.
Please write the correct spelling on this form.
We need to compare it with your identification.
The corrected card will be printed while you wait.
There is no fee because the office made the original error.
Check your full name and birth date carefully before accepting the new card.
We will destroy the incorrect card after the updated one has been added to the system.

sets.context: A visitor confirms a service appointment using a reference number.

sentences.text: Your appointment number begins with the letter B.
Enter the full number on the check-in screen.
Your name should appear with the scheduled time.
Take the printed ticket and wait in the blue area.
A staff member will call the ticket number, not your name.
If the screen cannot find the appointment, show the confirmation message at the information desk.
Visitors arriving more than fifteen minutes late may need to select another available time.

sets.context: A resident requests a stamped copy of a completed form.

sentences.text: We can make a stamped copy of your form.
First, submit the signed original at window three.
The clerk will check that every page is complete.
Your copy receives the same date as the original.
A stamped copy costs two dollars and can be paid by card.
Keep it as proof of submission because the full review may take several weeks.
Request both stamped copies before the original enters our filing system when two agencies need them.

sets.context: A driver asks the local office to review a parking notice.

sentences.text: You can ask us to review this parking notice.
Complete the short form on the city website.
Include the notice number and your vehicle plate.
You may upload photos or a parking payment receipt.
The review team normally replies within ten working days.
You do not have to pay while the review is open, but keep the original notice.
The reply will explain the payment deadline and appeal options if the request is refused.

sets.context: A resident registers a pet and collects a numbered tag.

sentences.text: Every dog in town needs a registration tag.
Bring proof of the current vaccination.
The clerk will record your address and phone number.
Your numbered tag is ready as soon as you pay.
Attach it to the dog’s collar whenever you are outside home.
Registration lasts one year, and we will send a renewal notice before it expires.
We can replace it without repeating the full registration process if the tag is lost.

sets.context: A resident renews a local identification card.

sentences.text: Your resident card expires at the end of November.
You may renew it up to one month early.
Bring the current card and one address document.
We will take a new photograph at the counter.
The renewal fee can be paid by cash or card.
Your old card remains valid until the replacement arrives in about ten days.
Tell the clerk about upcoming travel plans because the replacement card may arrive later than expected.

sets.context: A club member asks whether a small project can receive local support.

sentences.text: Small community projects may apply for this grant.
Your club must serve people in the local area.
Funding can cover materials, room rental, and public signs.
It cannot be used to pay regular club members.
Applications need a simple budget and a short project description.
Before applying, attend the online information session to ask questions about eligible costs.
Projects beginning before the decision date cannot receive funding from the current grant round.

sets.context: A visitor requests a nonprivate record from a town office.

sentences.text: This office provides copies of nonprivate public records.
Describe the document and approximate date on this form.
A specific request helps us search more quickly.
We will contact you if any part contains private information.
Small electronic files are usually sent by email without a fee.
Large requests may take longer and require payment for staff time or printed pages.
You can narrow the date range later if the first search finds too many records.

sets.context: A tenant tests a smoke alarm and reports a weak battery.

sentences.text: Press the smoke alarm button for three seconds.
A loud sound means the alarm is working.
This short beep usually indicates a weak battery.
Write down which room has the problem alarm.
The building manager can bring a replacement battery this afternoon.
Until it is replaced, do not remove the alarm or cover the sound opening.
Leave the apartment and call emergency services if you smell smoke or hear a continuous alarm.

sets.context: Roommates label food in a shared refrigerator.

sentences.text: Please label food kept in the shared refrigerator.
Write your name and the date on each container.
Blue labels are in the drawer beside the sink.
Use the top shelf for food you plan to share.
Personal items should stay on your assigned refrigerator shelf.
Every Sunday evening, we will throw away anything expired or left without a label.
Message the group before the weekly cleaning if you want to save an unlabeled item.

sets.context: A resident protects a package expected during wet weather.

sentences.text: A package is expected while it is raining tomorrow.
Please select the covered side entrance for delivery.
Leave that gate unlocked between noon and three.
A dry storage box is beside the side door.
Add a delivery note asking the driver to close the lid.
If the parcel needs a signature, the driver cannot leave it in the box unattended.
You can track the arrival time and move the package indoors as soon as it is delivered.

sets.context: A neighbor arranges to return a borrowed ladder.

sentences.text: I can return your ladder on Saturday morning.
It is still stored in my garage.
I cleaned the steps after finishing the work.
Please tell me whether you will be home around ten.
If not, I can leave it behind your garden gate.
The ladder is too long for my car, so I will carry it over with a neighbor.
Before I bring it, I will check the locking bar because it felt slightly stiff yesterday.

sets.context: A traveler leaves simple plant-care directions for a friend.

sentences.text: Please water the plants on Wednesday and Saturday.
The small can is under the kitchen sink.
Give the cactus only a little water.
The two herbs by the window dry out more quickly.
Move the fern away from direct afternoon sunlight if the room gets hot.
There is no need to add plant food because I used it just before leaving.
Remove fallen leaves from the shelf so they do not stay damp beneath the pots.

sets.context: A neighbor collects a spare key before walking a dog.

sentences.text: This spare key opens both the gate and front door.
The dog’s leash hangs beside the coat rack.
Take him out around eight each morning.
His usual route goes through the park and back along Pine Street.
Use the shorter route if the pavement is hot or icy.
After the walk, refill his water bowl and lock the gate from the inside.
Show him the small treat kept in your jacket pocket if he refuses to come home.

sets.context: Housemates agree on times for using a shared washing machine.

sentences.text: The washing machine is busiest on weekend mornings.
I will use it Saturday from nine to eleven.
You can take the next time period before lunch.
Please remove clothes soon after your wash cycle finishes.
The quiet setting should be used after eight in the evening.
If someone finishes early, they can post a message so the machine becomes available sooner.
Wet clothes left inside for more than thirty minutes may be moved to the clean basket.

sets.context: A family member leaves a reminder about a pharmacy pickup.

sentences.text: Your medicine is ready at the neighborhood pharmacy.
Please collect it before six this evening.
Bring your identification and the pickup message.
The pharmacist may ask whether you take any other medicine.
Check the name and instructions on the label before leaving.
If the cost is different from last time, ask the pharmacist to explain the change.
The medicine needs refrigeration, so come straight home or carry it in the small cooler.

sets.context: A host prepares clean bedding for a weekend guest.

sentences.text: Clean sheets are folded on the spare bed.
Two pillows are stored in the closet.
Put the fitted sheet on the mattress first.
The striped cover belongs inside the white blanket case.
Leave an extra towel on the chair near the window.
Since the nights are cooler now, add the gray blanket at the foot of the bed.
Before the guest arrives, open the window briefly and make sure the bedside lamp works.

sets.context: Housemates prepare sorted recycling for an early collection.

sentences.text: Recycling is collected early tomorrow morning.
The sorted bags are beside the back door.
Glass belongs in the small blue container.
Flatten the cardboard so everything fits inside the large bin.
Rinse food containers and remove any plastic film or lids.
Put the recycling outside tonight because the truck sometimes arrives before seven.
Save the extra cardboard for next week’s collection if the bin is too full to close.
